candidate.title: fC-Seal
candidate.scope: The single fC-Seal row of the assigned Illumina poster schematic: selective labeling and capture of DNA bearing 5-formylcytosine, from cytosine-modified genomic DNA through released enriched DNA. The left-side 5fc residue icon and description summarize the target rather than defining a second input. The complete attached image also shows separate Aba-seq, TAmC-Seq and fC-CET rows; none is an alternative or connected branch of the fC-Seal row. The matching secondary catalogue page is headed fC-Seal and captions the same reaction route. The Song et al. primary paper resolves the blocking/reduction logic. hMe-Seal is a cited labeling component, and fCAB-Seq is a separate unshown workflow, so neither expands method_names. Sequencing is used to interpret the DNA output; its library preparation is not decomposed into unshown steps.

states.label: Genomic DNA fragments bearing 5fC and other cytosine states
features: The row depicts C, 5mC, 5hmC, 5fC and 5caC along the same illustrative DNA backbone.
The separate left-side 5fc residue icon summarizes the biological target; it is not an additional input branch.
The primary implementation uses fragmented duplex genomic DNA. The row specifies no adapters, barcodes or DNA end groups and does not depict fragmentation as a local operation.

operations.label: βGT-catalyzed glucosylation
operations.description: Glucosylate pre-existing DNA 5hmC with unmodified glucose, producing blocked 5hmC while leaving the target 5fC available for the next step.
operations.mechanism: β-glucosyltransferase (βGT) catalyzes glucose transfer to 5hmC; the paper identifies unmodified glucose as the blocking modification.
operations.information_effect: Marks the preparation history of native 5hmC so it is excluded from subsequent labeling of newly generated 5hmC.

operations.label: NaBH4; Convert 5fc to 5hmc
operations.description: Reduce original 5fC in the blocked DNA to 5hmC, producing a newly labelable hydroxymethyl substrate at those genomic positions.
operations.mechanism: NaBH4-mediated reduction of 5fC to 5hmC. The paper reports resistance of protected 5hmC, 5mC and 5caC to this reduction under its conditions.
operations.information_effect: Converts a 5fC identity into a selectively labelable 5hmC identity without changing the genomic sequence carrier.

operations.label: Streptavidin pulldown and DTT cleavage
operations.description: Capture the biotin-tagged DNA with streptavidin and cleave the depicted reducible linkage with DTT to yield released, enriched DNA. The shared caption is retained as one composite operation.
